question: Nursing informatics brings together three major fields. Which ones are they?
explanation: Think of nursing informatics as a sweet spot where nursing care meets computer technology and data management to help us handle health information smoothly! [learn more](GNS113_U1_T1#GNS113_U1_T1_h1)

question: What is the main reason we use nursing informatics in our hospitals and clinics?

options.A: To replace bedside nurses with automated robots
options.B: To increase the paperwork required for admission
options.C: To support and improve patient care delivery
options.D: To reduce hospital spending on medical equipment

explanation: At the end of the day, all these tech tools and systems are here to help us take better, safer care of our patients. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T1#GNS113_U1_T1_h1)

question: You just took a patient's temperature and wrote down a single number. What do we call this raw, unorganized fact?
explanation: Raw, unprocessed facts and figures—like a lone temperature reading—are known as data before we connect them to other clues. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T1#GNS113_U1_T1_h2)

question: Using your clinical experience and recognizing patterns to choose the best care for a patient shows what level of thinking?
explanation: Spot on! Wisdom is that highest level where you combine knowledge with your clinical experience to make sound, safe decisions for your patients. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T1#GNS113_U1_T1_h2)

question: Back when healthcare facilities first started using computers, what was their main job?
explanation: Hospitals originally brought in computers to handle business office tasks and billing long before they were used directly at the bedside. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T1#GNS113_U1_T1_h3)

question: Why did early hospital computer systems often drive clinical nurses crazy?

options.A: They completely eliminated the need for nursing notes
options.B: They required patients to input their own medical history
options.C: They were too portable and easily lost on the ward
options.D: They created extra administrative work instead of helping care

explanation: Those early systems were built for accountants, not nurses! They made charting feel like an extra burden rather than a help to patient care. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T1#GNS113_U1_T1_h3)

question: What is the main role of a nursing informaticist on the hospital team?

options.A: To act as a bridge between clinical nurses and the IT department
options.B: to manage the hospital kitchen and catering staff
options.C: To work with external pharmaceutical suppliers
options.D: To assist government tax collection agencies

explanation: Informaticists speak 'nursing' and 'tech'! They help translate what nurses need at the bedside into instructions that computer developers can actually build. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T1#GNS113_U1_T1_h4)

question: Your hospital is launching a new electronic medication system. Who is the best person to train the ward nurses?
explanation: Because nursing informaticists understand both clinical ward life and software, they are the absolute best people to guide nurses through new tech. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T1#GNS113_U1_T1_h4)

question: Why do electronic health records rely on standardized nursing terms?

options.A: To prevent doctors from viewing patient vital sign charts
options.B: To replace medical diagnoses with nursing terminology entirely
options.C: To make nursing documentation twice as long to complete
options.D: To allow clear communication and data sharing across systems

explanation: When we all use the same agreed-upon terms, different computers and health workers can understand patient problems and care plans without any confusion. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T1#GNS113_U1_T1_h5)

question: Which of these is NOT a recognized standardized nursing terminology?
explanation: You got it! Financial reporting standards are used in business and accounting, not for clinical nursing care. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T1#GNS113_U1_T1_h5)

question: What is a major danger when an electronic health record system bombards nurses with too many repetitive pop-up warnings?

options.A: Computers will automatically shut down due to processor overload
options.B: Patients will gain direct access to physician prescription pads
options.C: Hospital electricity bills will increase dramatically
options.D: Nurses may experience alert fatigue and ignore important warnings

explanation: It's the 'boy who cried wolf' effect! When minor pop-ups happen constantly, busy nurses might click past them and accidentally miss a life-saving warning. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T1#GNS113_U1_T1_h6)

question: How does scanning medication barcodes at the bedside help keep patients safe?

options.A: It updates the hospital room cleaning schedule
options.B: It checks the nurse's monthly salary scale
options.C: It verifies the right patient, drug, and dose
options.D: It tracks the patient's insurance coverage limit

explanation: Barcode scanning is a brilliant safety net—it matches the patient's wristband with the drug package right before you give it, preventing medication errors. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T1#GNS113_U1_T1_h6)

question: What is one of the biggest hurdles to running electronic health record systems smoothly in many Nigerian healthcare facilities?

options.A: Nurses refusing to learn how to read or write
options.B: Unstable power supply and infrastructure limits
options.C: Laws banning computers inside hospital wards
options.D: An absolute lack of patients needing admission

explanation: Reliable electricity and internet access are still major daily challenges for digital health setups in many of our local facilities. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T1#GNS113_U1_T1_h7)

question: If a nurse is working in a remote rural clinic and needs advice from a city specialist, what technology makes this possible?
explanation: Telemedicine is a game-changer! It connects rural healthcare workers and patients directly with urban specialists using phones and internet tools. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T1#GNS113_U1_T1_h7)
